# Copying models {#sec-copy}

A program copies a model to change it without touching the original, or to give it to another thread ([Threads](#sec-threads)). The copy holds the same variables, functions, constraints and objectives, under the same indices. A change to one never reaches the other.

## Copying {#sec-copy-c}

`BIYOS_copymdl` copies a model onto an environment, its own or another:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/copies.c" item="copy_and_change"}
```

The copy belongs to the environment it was made on and reports there. It keeps the options set on its source and reads the others from its environment. It shares the callbacks of its source, with the same `data`, so `data` must stay alive while either model can call them. It has none of the source's hooks. See [`BIYOS_copymdl`](#BIYOS_copymdl) for the full rules.

## Comparing {#sec-copy-compare}

`BIYOS_cmpmdl` tells whether two models hold the same problem. When they differ, it sends the first difference as an info message ([The events biyos sends](#sec-events-sent)). In Python, `Model.compare` returns that text.

Numbers match bit for bit, so `0.0` and `-0.0` differ. The example compares the bounds of the copy with those of the source:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/copies.c" item="same_bounds"}
```

Unlike `BIYOS_cmpmdl`, `<` and `>` treat `0.0` and `-0.0` as equal.
